title: Iteration-counts Lemma case (P): heuristic proof, wrong per-step claim

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Critical rigor gap in the 'Iteration counts' Lemma, case (P)** (engine for families (a) and (h)).

Case (P) claims: $N(x)/(x/\log x)\in[\tfrac12,2]$ for large $x$ $\Rightarrow$ $T(n)=(1+o(1))\log n/\log\log n$.

The proof is heuristic and partly wrong:
1. It asserts 'each step decreases $\ell_j=\log x_j$ by $(1+o(1))\log\log n$ while $x_j\in[n^{1/2},n]$'. This is false: the per-step decrement is $\log\ell_j$, which is NOT constant over the orbit; it changes by a bounded factor only over a single dyadic block of $\ell$, not across the whole descent.
2. The 'convergent geometric-type series' claim is not a derivation.
3. There is no control of the tail once $x_j$ becomes small, where $N(x)/x \asymp 1/\log x$ fails (e.g. $\pi$ at small arguments).

**The leading-order conclusion is in fact correct** — the true step count equals $\mathrm{li}(\log n)(1+o(1)) = \frac{\log n}{\log\log n}(1+o(1))$ — but the convergence is logarithmically slow (numerically the idealized map $x\mapsto x/\log x$ gives $\approx 1.27\cdot\log n/\log\log n$ at $n=10^{256}$). A correct proof should: set $\ell_j=\log x_j$, show $\ell_{j+1}=\ell_j-\log\ell_j+o(\log\ell_j)$ uniformly, sandwich the recursion between the maps $x\mapsto x/((1\pm\epsilon)\log x)$, compare with the ODE $\ell'=-\log\ell$ whose hitting time is $\mathrm{li}(\ell_0)$, and bound the bounded $O(1)$ tail through small $x$ separately.
